title: Air India Express Unveils Massive Gulf Expansion, Plans 150-Aircraft Fleet by 2028
excerpt: The Tata-owned budget carrier targets new routes to Abu Dhabi, Jeddah, and Muscat as it bets on the India-Gulf travel corridor serving 9 million NRIs.
body:
• Air India Express has unveiled aggressive West Asia expansion plans, targeting new routes across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Oman to serve the 9-million-strong Indian diaspora in the Gulf.
  • The airline plans to nearly double its fleet from 88 to over 150 aircraft by 2028, making it one of India's fastest-growing carriers.
  • New routes to Abu Dhabi, Jeddah, and Muscat are expected to launch by early 2027, adding to existing hubs in Dubai, Sharjah, and Kuwait.
  • The expansion comes as Gulf airspace closures from the Iran conflict disrupted travel for millions of Indians across the Middle East.

Betting Big on the Gulf Corridor

Air India Express has revealed ambitious plans to expand its West Asia network, targeting the massive travel corridor between India and the Gulf that serves nearly 9 million Indian workers, professionals, and families living across the region. In an exclusive interview with NDTV, the airline's leadership outlined a strategy to nearly double its fleet and add new routes to key Gulf destinations by early 2027.

"For the millions of Indians whose lives straddle the Gulf and the subcontinent, more flights and lower fares translate directly into more time with family.</p>"

"For the millions of Indians whose lives straddle the Gulf and the subcontinent, more flights and lower fares translate directly into more time with family.</p>"

The budget carrier, part of the Tata Group's consolidated Air India aviation portfolio, currently operates 88 aircraft with connections to Dubai, Sharjah, Kuwait, and several other Gulf cities. The expansion will push the fleet past 150 aircraft by 2028 and add routes to Abu Dhabi, Jeddah, Muscat, and Dammam — cities with large Indian populations that are currently underserved by direct budget connections from tier-2 Indian cities.

Serving a Diaspora Under Strain

The announcement carries particular weight given the recent disruption to Gulf travel caused by the Iran conflict. Airspace closures, flight cancellations, and rerouted services have hammered Indian workers across the Middle East, many of whom rely on affordable direct flights to maintain ties with families back home.

"Our goal is to ensure every Indian worker in the Gulf is one affordable, direct flight away from home."

— Air India Express Leadership

Air India Express has historically been the airline of choice for blue-collar and mid-tier Indian workers in the Gulf, offering lower fares than full-service carriers on routes between Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Gulf cities. The expansion into Saudi Arabia and Oman acknowledges a shift in India's Gulf migration patterns, with more workers heading to these markets as the UAE's economy matures.

Fleet Growth and Competition

The fleet expansion from 88 to 150-plus aircraft will be fueled by Boeing 737 MAX deliveries already on order as part of the Tata Group's massive aircraft procurement. Air India Express will also absorb routes from AIX Connect, the former AirAsia India, as the Tata aviation consolidation continues.

The airline faces stiff competition from IndiGo, which has aggressively expanded its own Gulf network, and from Gulf carriers like Air Arabia and flydubai that offer competitive fares on India-bound routes. Air India Express's advantage lies in its Indian origin — many Gulf-based workers prefer dealing with an Indian carrier for language, food, and baggage allowance considerations.

What's Next

The first new Gulf routes are expected to launch in early 2027, with Abu Dhabi and Jeddah as priority additions. The airline is also exploring connections from northeast Indian cities to the Gulf, targeting a growing worker population from states like Manipur and Nagaland that currently lacks direct access. For the millions of Indians whose lives straddle the Gulf and the subcontinent, more flights and lower fares translate directly into more time with family.
